newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares fall victim to profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares fall victim to profit-taking.

text.p: Profit-takers put an end to a two-day rally, driving Delhi shares sharply lower in early afternoon trade on Wednesday, traders said.

The Delhi Stock Exchange's benchmark index was down 7.35 points at 950.20 at 12:45 p.m. (0715 GMT). The index had been up 3.93 points at 961.48 in early trade after rising nearly five percent over the previous two sessions.
"The market opened with overnight strength but profit-taker pressure wiped out earlier gains in most of the key stocks," Ashok Arya of stock brokers S.C. Gupta said.
Hindustan Lever, which had surged on Tuesday after announcing a 39 percent rise in first half net profit, lost 13.50 rupees to 1,532.
State Bank of India lost 1.75 rupees to 337.50.
Bucking the trend, TISCO added 2.65 rupees to 226 and TELCO gained three rupees to 402.20.
Larsen and Toubro shed 3.45 rupees to 281.
